Global ProductStateProjection, product-completeness or closure semantics.

constraints: Dependency edge is not work ordering.
Invalidation is not organization or workflow-stage reset.
Product semantic lineage and Blackboard work lifecycle are distinct state spaces.
Claim authority, execution policy and domain write authority do not imply one another.
Historical accepted claims and obligations remain reconstructable after becoming stale, revoked or superseded.
Container revision alone is not sufficient authority to invalidate unrelated semantic subjects.
Semantic equivalence guessed by an LLM cannot prune required invalidation in the first implementation slice.
invariants: Board dependency DAG != product semantic lineage
claim authority != execution policy != domain write authority
historical claim validity != currentness for new mutation
no LLM semantic guess may prune required invalidation in v1
architectureDecisions: CrossDomainObligation is an immutable WHAT contract from one accepted semantic publication to another domain; it contains target domain/workload and required outcome, never worker identity, runtime, strategy or priority.

Domain write authority is a separate CAS-headed authority surface. A production publication gate implements the existing DomainExecutionController publicationGate interface instead of introducing a second execution controller.

DomainExecutionController remains the generic post-claim HOW boundary. SA execution is selected later from SA-owned ExecutionPolicy and immutable ExecutionStrategyDescriptor; Integration C does not add an SA-specific scheduler or hard-coded execution strategy module.

Only a trusted accepted DomainPublicationReceipt may commit SemanticClaim revisions, CrossDomainObligation revisions and ProductDerivationEdge records into authoritative product truth; runtime proposedDerivationEdges remain proposals until publication.

SemanticClaim and CrossDomainObligation payloads are immutable. Separate CAS currentness heads point to the current revision and record ACTIVE, STALE, REVOKED or SUPERSEDED transitions without mutating historical evidence.

Logical obligation identity is normalized from project/root intent, issuing semantic subject, target domain/workload, obligation kind and stable obligation key. Replaying identical normalized content converges on one immutable revision; changed semantic content creates a new revision and supersedes the prior current head.

ProductDerivationEdge is a product-semantic dependency, not a Blackboard dependency. Reverse adjacency/impact indexes are rebuildable accelerators; immutable publication receipts, semantic revisions, edges and head transitions remain authority.

Selective invalidation starts from exact superseded semantic subject keys and follows reverse-transitive authoritative ProductDerivationEdge closure. Only impacted claim/obligation heads transition non-current; unrelated siblings remain current.

Dependent publication uses a two-observation currentness handshake: capture every consumed semantic-head revision before publication, persist the publication under the guarded write-authority/lifecycle window, then revalidate those exact observations before the dependent head can remain current. Drift forces deterministic stale reconciliation.

Cross-domain work materialization consumes an exact ACTIVE CrossDomainObligation revision plus its issuance/publication authority and existing materialization authorization. Stale/revoked/superseded obligations fail closed before new work can be created.

When an obligation becomes non-current, only Board work materialized from that exact obligation subject is affected. READY/REOPENED work is blocked; claimed/released work is invalidated through the existing organization claim lifecycle so executable capability is fenced before it can continue.
No LLM semantic-equivalence decision participates in invalidation pruning for v1. Precision comes from explicit stable semantic subject keys and accepted derivation edges.
implementationSlices: C1 — production domain write authority: implement DomainWriteAuthorityPolicy/current CAS head plus a trusted publication gate adapter for the existing DomainExecutionController; bind publisher principal/domain/allowed semantic and obligation kinds and preserve the current organization lifecycle publication fence.

C2 — immutable semantic subjects: implement content-addressed SemanticClaim and CrossDomainObligation revisions with separate CAS currentness heads, normalized logical keys, idempotent identical replay and explicit supersession/revocation transitions.

C3 — authoritative product lineage: persist ProductDerivationEdge only from accepted DomainPublicationReceipt publication, maintain rebuildable reverse-impact indexes, and implement deterministic reverse-transitive DependencyImpactAnalysis over exact semantic subject keys.

C4 — currentness reconciliation and work invalidation: perform the pre/post consumed-head handshake, mark raced dependents non-current, reject stale obligation materialization, and map an invalidated obligation only to work materialized from that exact obligation subject using existing block/invalidate/fence lifecycle seams.

C5 — BA -> SA executable vertical: publish an accepted BA requirement claim, issue one authorized SA solution-design obligation, materialize deterministic SA-owned work, prove BA never chooses SA worker/runtime/strategy, and show SA execution mechanics remain resolved by existing ExecutionPolicy/ExecutionStrategyDescriptor infrastructure.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: An accepted BA requirement subject may issue an SA solution-design obligation only when the current DomainWriteAuthority authorizes that target domain and obligation kind.
evidenceRequired: Positive BA->SA authorization case plus rejected unauthorized target-domain/obligation-kind cases.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: One current authorized SA solution-design obligation revision materializes one deterministic SA-owned OrganizationWorkContract and Board work item.
evidenceRequired: Exact obligation revision -> deterministic SA-owned work identity assertion.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The BA domain never selects SA worker identity, runtime, execution strategy or priority when issuing the SA obligation.
evidenceRequired: Negative assertions showing no worker/runtime/strategy/priority fields or SA execution-selection call originate from BA.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: An accepted SA publication may commit an architecture SemanticClaim only when the current DomainWriteAuthority permits that semantic kind.
evidenceRequired: Allowed architecture semantic-kind publication plus rejected disallowed semantic-kind publication.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: An accepted SA publication may commit a CrossDomainObligation only when the current DomainWriteAuthority permits that obligation kind and target domain.
evidenceRequired: Allowed obligation publication plus rejected disallowed obligation-kind/target-domain publication.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Only an accepted DomainPublicationReceipt may create authoritative SemanticClaim revisions, CrossDomainObligation revisions or ProductDerivationEdge records.
evidenceRequired: Forged/raw publication input cannot create authoritative product records; accepted receipt can.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Superseding one detail requirement makes every reverse-transitive authoritative semantic dependent of that exact subject non-current.
evidenceRequired: Reverse-transitive invalidation log from the changed detail subject to its exact dependents.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Superseding one detail requirement leaves semantic subjects and work outside its authoritative reverse-transitive closure current.
evidenceRequired: Sibling/list semantic heads and unrelated work remain current/executable after the targeted supersession.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A dependent publication that observes upstream supersession between its pre-publication and post-publication currentness checks cannot remain current.
evidenceRequired: Barrier-controlled race proving post-observation drift deterministically marks/reconciles the dependent non-current.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Replaying identical normalized obligation content resolves to the same immutable obligation revision.
evidenceRequired: Repeated identical publication returns the same logical revision identity with no second current revision.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Repeated materialization of the same current obligation revision resolves to the same deterministic target work identity.
evidenceRequired: Repeated materialization does not create duplicate SA work.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Changing normalized obligation semantics creates a new immutable revision that supersedes the prior revision without mutating it.
evidenceRequired: Semantic-change publication creates a distinct revision; prior revision bytes remain unchanged and historical.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A STALE, REVOKED or SUPERSEDED obligation revision cannot materialize new target work.
evidenceRequired: Materialization rejects each non-current status before creating a Board item.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Already-claimed work sourced from an obligation that becomes non-current loses executable capability through canonical organization-claim invalidation and fencing.
evidenceRequired: Affected claimed work is invalidated/fenced and cannot continue execution.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A fresh store can reconstruct semantic currentness heads, obligation currentness heads and authoritative product lineage from immutable authoritative records.
evidenceRequired: Fresh-store replay reconstructs the same current heads and authoritative derivation edges.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Deleting disposable reverse-impact indexes does not change reconstructed semantic currentness or dependency impact.
evidenceRequired: Rebuild after cache/index deletion yields identical currentness and impact closure.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: CrossDomainObligation construction rejects worker identity, runtime, execution strategy and priority fields.
evidenceRequired: Constructor/schema negative cases reject each dispatch-mechanics field.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: ProductDerivationEdge state cannot control Blackboard work ordering.
evidenceRequired: Changing ProductDerivationEdge fixtures does not create or reorder Blackboard dependency edges.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Selective invalidation never invokes an organization-wide or workflow-stage reset.
evidenceRequired: Instrumentation proves only exact impacted semantic heads/work items receive invalidation actions.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Blackboard dependency edges are never interpreted as ProductDerivationEdge semantic lineage.
evidenceRequired: Separate graph fixtures prove Board dependencies alone produce no semantic invalidation.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Runtime proposedDerivationEdges cannot become authoritative ProductDerivationEdge records without an accepted DomainPublicationReceipt.
evidenceRequired: Raw/forged proposed lineage remains non-authoritative; accepted publication persists lineage.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Organization claim authority cannot authorize an execution strategy selection.
evidenceRequired: Claim authority presented as execution-policy authority is rejected.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: ExecutionPolicy authority cannot authorize a domain semantic write.
evidenceRequired: Execution policy presented as DomainWriteAuthority is rejected.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: DomainWriteAuthority cannot authorize organization claim or execution capability.
evidenceRequired: Domain write authority presented as claim/execution authority is rejected.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A historical accepted claim or obligation revision remains resolvable after its currentness head moves away from that revision.
evidenceRequired: Historical immutable revision remains readable after STALE/SUPERSEDED transition.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A non-current historical claim or obligation revision cannot authorize a new mutation.
evidenceRequired: Mutation/materialization using the historical non-current revision fails closed.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Dependency invalidation closure is computed only from explicit semantic subject keys and accepted authoritative edges.
evidenceRequired: No model/equivalence callback exists in the pruning path and all required explicit edges are traversed.

negativeVerificationCases: A BA publication that requests an obligation kind or target domain outside current DomainWriteAuthority is rejected before an obligation/head/work item is committed.
A CrossDomainObligation carrying worker identity, runtime, strategy or priority is rejected; the source domain cannot smuggle dispatch mechanics into WHAT.
Raw runtime proposedDerivationEdges without an accepted DomainPublicationReceipt never enter authoritative ProductDerivationEdge truth.
Replaying byte/semantic-equivalent normalized obligation publication does not create a second logical current revision or duplicate Board work.
Changing obligation semantics creates a new immutable revision and supersedes the prior head; the old historical revision remains resolvable.
Materialization from STALE, REVOKED or SUPERSEDED obligation currentness fails closed and creates no target work.
If an upstream subject changes while a dependent publication is in flight, the dependent cannot finish as silently current after the post-publication observation check.
Superseding one detail requirement invalidates only reverse-transitive detail/architecture dependents; an unrelated sibling/list claim remains ACTIVE and its work stays executable.
Blackboard task dependency edges alone never participate in product semantic invalidation.
Invalidation never resets the whole organization/stage and never reopens unrelated Board work.
Already-claimed work sourced from an invalidated obligation loses executable capability through canonical organization-claim invalidation/release fencing.
No model-produced semantic-equivalence guess may remove an edge or prune a required invalidation path.

objectiveCoverage.objectiveCriterion: Accepted BA requirement can create only an authorized SA solution-design obligation and deterministic SA-owned work without selecting SA execution mechanics.
Accepted SA output can publish architecture subjects and only obligation kinds allowed by current domain write authority.
Changing one detail requirement invalidates only exact semantic dependents and leaves unrelated claims/work current.
A racing dependent publication cannot remain silently current after upstream supersession.
Identical normalized obligation replay is idempotent; semantic change supersedes immutably.
Stale/revoked obligations cannot materialize new work and already-claimed affected work is fenced.
Authoritative lineage/currentness is reconstructable without disposable impact caches.

verificationScopeNote: BB-052 uses criterion-specific Integration C checks plus the full agentic regression suite. The workspace-wide npm run verify command is intentionally not the semantic feature gate because unrelated package/evaluation failures must not be mistaken for Integration C evidence; normal repository CI remains an independent regression signal.
